sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Private Network and Digital Encryption Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–Netherlands Tax Treaty (pending entry into force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Prevención de Lavado de Activos y Financiamiento del Terrorismo), as amended; Ley No. 70 de 2019 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 406 de 2019 and implementing regulations; Reglamento de la Ley No. 23 (normas AML/CFT).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (full legible pages)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of current residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Bank reference letter or professional due diligence form (KYC)
Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate legal holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the legal holder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and foundation council members against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Panama's preventive list, and national PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or VPN/digital asset-related activity. Continuous transaction monitoring and ad-hoc re-screening apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sistema de Envíos Electrónicos (SEE) / Oficina de Nombre Comercial (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All foundation names must be expressed in Latin script; if the proposed name is in a non-Latin script, a certified transliteration into Spanish is required. The name may include words in any language, but must avoid confusion with existing registered entities and must not mislead the public about the entity's legal structure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may, within 20 business days of notification, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá. The request must cite the specific grounds for reversal, include any supporting legal precedent or trademark documentation, and be filed by a licensed attorney. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the Plenary Board of the Registro Público, and subsequently to the First Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court if administratively exhausted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for the statutory registered-agent address subject to acceptance by the licensed registered agent. For the operational stage, a virtual office is acceptable for a VPN Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business, provided that the company maintains substantive contractual, banking, and administrative records through its registered agent. Minimal physical presence requirements may be imposed by AML auditors, however, no statutory mandate for an operational office exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (10-15% annual probability) triggered by UBO verification or AML/CFT risk-based supervision, mainly through inspection of the registered agent's records rather than the foundation's own physical premises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foundation name reservation and search fee
Registry registration fee for Private Interest Foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on capital range

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal fee for drafting foundation charter and council regulations
AML/KYC and UBO due diligence package (founder, council, beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for enhanced due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille certification of origin documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and Ministry of Government/General Directorate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Security and courier delivery of original documents
Contingency for administrative fees and fiscal stamp

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 concerning Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 13 of 1997, and Executive Decree No. 15 of 1996; constitutional provisions at Articles 1-8, registered office and legal representation at Articles 13-22, and mandatory Foundation Charter contents at Articles 18-25.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Personas Jurídicas Section, Foundations Sub-Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Constitutiva de la Fundación) together with Foundation Regulations (Reglamento), executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up endowment is fixed under Law No. 25 of 1995; the Foundation Charter must identify the initial endowment contributed by the Founder, which may consist of cash, rights or in-kind assets. No escrow bank account or deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial endowment of USD 10,000 described in the Foundation Charter be accepted and recorded by the Foundation Council, and the Founder's subscription to the foundation assets is approved. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation be established at the address of the Registered Agent in Panama City, Panama, and that the Registered Agent be authorized to receive official notices and legal process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons named in the Foundation Charter are appointed as President, Secretary and Treasurer of the Foundation Council, with authority to implement all acts permitted by Law No. 25 of 1995. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers are authorized to sign banking, commercial and administrative documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public; support by the Foundation's Registered Agent and licensed Panamanian counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panama-licensed attorney or licensed Registered Agent. Prepare the draft Foundation Charter containing the foundation name, purposes, initial endowment, Foundation Council members, registered office clause and beneficiary provisions. Confirm name availability through the Public Registry and then arrange execution of the Charter and any separate Regulations before a Panamanian Notary Public. The notary protocols the instrument and returns photostatic copies for submission to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity document of the Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Registered Agent raises a documentary or AML query, correct the draft or supply clarified beneficiary and source-of-funds evidence, then re-execute the instrument before the same or another Notary Public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Personas Jurídicas Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter and any separate Regulations to the Public Registry together with the official inscribing application and proof of payment of registry fees. The Registry verifies the legality of the object, the uniqueness of the foundation name and the identity of the Registered Agent. Upon inscription, the Foundation acquires separate legal personality and the Registry generates an official inscription number and registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to any 'prevención' or clarification order issued by the Registrar within ten business days; correct defects, file additional evidence, or, if the foundation name conflicts, approve an alternate name and amend the Charter before re-inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foundation Registration Certificate and Ratify Appointed Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama; Foundation's Registered Agent office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the official Certificate of Registration of the Foundation from the Public Registry. Convene the Founder and initial Foundation Council to adopt the first resolution ratifying the registered office, accepting the endowment and appointing the President, Secretary and Treasurer. Record the resolution in the Foundation's corporate minutes and retain the minutes at the Registered Agent's office. Distribute the certificate and powers of representation to the appointed officers.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity documents of appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry certificate contains discrepancies, file a written correction term and obtain a revised certificate; if officer acceptance documentation is incomplete, obtain new acceptance letters or appoint replacement officers by a further council resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation for Tax, Beneficial Ownership and Data Privacy Purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos - DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the DGI for the Foundation's RUC tax identification number and register the beneficial ownership information in the official private beneficial ownership registry. If the VPN and privacy application generates Panama-source revenue, register for ITBMS and electronic invoicing; if all operations are foreign-source, file the appropriate tax deregistration or non-taxable status. If personal data is processed in or targeted to Panama, register the data processing activities with ANTAI under Panama's Law No. 81 of 2019.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI returns the application for clarification, provide amended beneficial ownership schedules or proof of foreign-source income within ten business days; if ANTAI requests data mapping, submit the privacy impact assessment and modify the processing register accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Aviso de Operación and Zoning Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá), Municipal Treasury and Licensing Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the Foundation maintains a physical office, commercial establishment or any operational presence in Panama, file the municipal Aviso de Operación, obtain the zoning and urban compatibility certificate and pay the annual municipal patent fee. For a purely remote SaaS/VPN operation with no Panamanian operational premises, the registered office alone does not require a municipal commercial license; nevertheless, the Foundation should document that status in its corporate file to avoid assumed local presence.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title for operational premises
Fire inspection certificate for physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality questions the Aviso de Operación, submit the corrected lease, zoning certificate or a revised declaration of no local operational presence and pay any adjusted municipal fee within fifteen business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Industrial, Environmental and Civil Defense Screening for the Digital Services Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI); Ministry of Environment (MiAMBIENTE); Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministry of Health (MINSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because ISIC 6201 VPN and privacy software is an electronically delivered service and not industrial manufacturing, no industrial manufacturing permit is required. File a low-impact environmental classification/registration with MiAMBIENTE covering office operations and e-waste from IT equipment. Obtain a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for any physical office and an MINSA occupational health clearance for workplaces. Maintain personal data privacy documentation and network security records as part of the VPN application's operational compliance.
required_dossiers: E-waste disposal or authorized recycler contract
MINSA occupational health and structural load declaration
ANTAI privacy registration and data processing documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE requires a preliminary authorization because of data-center scale or uninterruptible power supply equipment, submit the supplemental environmental and generator emission documents; remedy any fire-safety or occupational deficiencies identified by the inspectors before re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias - MICI), General Directorate of Industry and Small Business
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación municipal; alternatively, for the digital service activity, a Non-Industrial Use Clearance for Electronically Delivered Software Services; no factory or manufacturing permit applies to ISIC 6201

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente - MiAMBIENTE), Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration, Category I-A (low adverse environmental impact); no full EIA report is required for a software/VPN service without industrial effluent, process emissions or hazardous manufacturing waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions; office-generated e-waste must be delivered to authorized recyclers; backup generator and HVAC emissions, if any, must comply with MiAMBIENTE air quality thresholds; solid waste segregation and minimum occupational noise exposure limits apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load inspection and occupational workplace health clearance from the Ministry of Health (MINSA); the Registered Agent-only office with no employees may be treated as a low-risk declared location requiring no fresh-air engineering inspection unless physical occupancy begins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portals: Sede Electrónica (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa) and institutional website (https://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Private Interest Foundation: (1) a resident registered agent (abogado/notario) executes the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) before a Notary Public; (2) the foundation deed is filed and registered in the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry, Private Interest Foundations Section); (3) the foundation council and resident agent are appointed; (4) obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) via the DGI Sede Electrónica by submitting the authenticated foundation deed, registered-agent certificate, fiscal-address proof, and identity documents of the founder, council members, and beneficiaries; (5) complete the municipal Aviso de Operación or consolidated DGI registration; (6) apply for ITBMS taxpayer status and electronic invoicing authorization. The DGI typically issues the Certificado de Registro del RUC within 10-15 business days; a PIF with no Panamanian-source activity remains registered but files nil returns as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' pass-through election exists under Panamanian law; a PIF is an opaque juridical person subject to tax only on Panama-source income. Available elections: (a) election to register and collect ITBMS as a taxable person for Panamanian-resident sales; (b) election to enter the simplified quota-based tax regime (Régimen Simplificado) for small taxpayers meeting DGI eligibility criteria; (c) election under Law 25 of 1995 to apply the foundation's statutory confidentiality protections and annual flat tax; (d) no domestic hybrid-mismatch election, though foreign jurisdictions may independently characterize the PIF as transparent or opaque under their own check-the-box or CFC rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — VAT-type transaction tax governed by the Código Fiscal and Ley 28 de 1995
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration is mandatory upon commencement of any taxable activity in Panamanian territory; there is no numeric turnover exemption threshold in the Código Fiscal. The local currency is the Balboa at parity with the US Dollar, and accounts are kept in USD. A small enterprise may apply to the DGI for Pequeño Contribuyente (simplified quota) status subject to the DGI's activity-volume limits, which substitutes full ITBMS returns with fixed periodic quotas.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing for all RUC holders: invoices must be issued through the DGI Sede Electrónica SV-T system under the Facturación Electrónica regime. The DGI must grant prior authorization for the invoice series/código de operación; invoices are transmitted in real time in DGI-specified XML format via web services/API; each fiscal document must display a QR code and digital stamp and receive DGI validation before being deemed authentic. The phased mandate is set out in DGI Resolution DGI-2019-0712 and subsequent implementation calendars.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies to exports: (i) tangible goods leaving Panamanian customs territory evidenced by a customs export declaration; and (ii) services, including digital VPN/network-security SaaS, where the recipient is domiciled outside Panama, the use or benefit of the service occurs entirely abroad, and the consideration is effectively remitted from abroad. The VPN privacy application qualifies for export zero-rating if invoiced to non-resident end users, delivered through international channels, and settled via foreign payment rails such as Stripe or Paymentwall; zero-rating is denied where services are supplied to persons located in Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Mercancías - DUA) for goods, or a formal service-export invoice with contractual description of offshore use for services
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods, or an electronic delivery/usage record for SaaS licensing
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by the collecting Panamanian bank, or PSP settlement statements proving remittance from abroad
Foreign-client affidavit or certificate confirming non-resident status and absence of Panamanian-source exploitation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits zero-rated export documentation retrospectively for up to six years; where substantiation is deficient, the supply is recharacterized as taxable locally: ITBMS is assessed with monthly interest, a surcharge of 100%-300% of the omitted tax, and administrative fines under the Código Fiscal, and wilful evasion may trigger criminal tax-fraud prosecution with imprisonment. Additionally, a PIF that misstates foreign-source service income risks clawback of the Law 25 of 1995 annual flat-tax benefits, loss of territorial exemption, and potential cancellation of foundation registration by the Public Registry for lack of legitimate economic purpose.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama operates no traditional central bank. Monetary stability derives from full dollarization, with the U.S. dollar as legal tender and the Panamanian balboa (USD 1:1) as nominal unit. Prudential banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); foreign-exchange policy and financial-stability coordination rest with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). The SBP implements AML/CFT Law 23 of 2015 and regulates all licensed banking activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current and capital account transactions. Panama imposes no exchange controls, no restrictions on the repatriation of equity, dividends, profits, or service fees, and no prior regulatory approval for cross-border capital flows. In practice, outbound remittances are subject to bank-level compliance verification (source of funds, sanctions screening, beneficial-ownership transparency) rather than government exchange control. The territorial taxation regime (taxed within Panama only) further facilitates clean profit remittance; a 5% dividend tax is withheld on distributions of Panamanian-source income, but VPN SaaS revenue earned globally outside Panama is generally outside scope.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama law does not mandate repatriation, surrender, or conversion of export or service receipts. VPN subscription and licensing proceeds receivable in USD, EUR, or other convertible currencies may be retained offshore or settled into Panamanian bank accounts without a statutory timeline or conversion minimum. The SBP, however, expects inflows to be reconciled against commercial invoices under the 2015 AML Due Diligence rules and the 2021 Beneficial Ownership regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency settlement) and segregated Capital Escrow Account for the PIF's initial endowment
Operational Account / Escrow Account for collected SaaS subscription flows routed via Paymentwall
Operational Account with Tier-1 correspondent access (USD clearing via Fedwire/CHIPS)
Operational Account and FX hedge line for EUR/GBP-denominated trade disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - Feasible subject to regulation. Panama's Financial Technology Law 169 of 2020 permits authorized fintech/electronic-money institutions to operate under SBP/SMV oversight, but offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not exempt from licensing and cannot autonomously acquire local account or clearing access. Recommended approach is a branchless EMI license through a local partner bank, or use of an SBP-licensed payment processor as a wiring agent rather than direct EMI onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default requirement. Under SBP AML/CFT Rule 2015-004, the foundation's initial directors and material beneficiaries must generally attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Panamanian branch, with signature verification before a Panamanian notary. Remote onboarding is permitted only where the client has an existing banking relationship, or where a qualified Panamanian counsel holds an approved power of attorney, and is then conditioned on enhanced due diligence, a live video call, and certified apostilled documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PA_PIF foundation vehicle flagged as an opaque private foundation (no public beneficial-ownership registry)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter (Spanish-notarized) and apostilled; certified registry certificate from the Public Registry of Panama naming the Resident Agent; private foundation deed disclosing the beneficiary in a sealed, lawfully protected annex; legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian attorney confirming lawful structure and beneficiary-control flow; sworn declaration of source of funds and the foundation's economic rationale for owning the VPN SaaS business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN network privacy app classified as 'Enhanced Risk' due to anonymity features and potential illicit-use profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial license and product specification; privacy policy and no-logging attestation; Acceptable Use Policy and jurisdiction-exclusion list; independent SOC 2 / ISO 27001 certificate; revenue model documents (Stripe/Paymentwall processing agreements) proving transparent subscription economics; batch transaction reconciliation of SaaS customer payments; completed AML self-risk assessment under SBP Guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident sole beneficiary and remote management from foreign jurisdiction creating a remote-management red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate resolutions and power of attorney; valid passport and residence permit of the opening agent or attorney-in-fact; six-month bank statements from the source of the endowment; original reference letter from the client's current correspondent bank (not older than 90 days); personal tax or wealth documentation demonstrating the legal source of the USD endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity subscription receipts via aggregators (Stripe/Paymentwall) potentially indicating unlicensed cross-border payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Paymentwall and Stripe; evidence that aggregator rails perform their own KYC on end customers; monthly settlement invoices and fee statements; contractual segregation of 'receivable for delivery of SaaS software' rather than payment-processing for third parties; revenue-recognition policy consistent with Panama's territorial tax regime.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial PIF endowment and recurring VPN SaaS receipts are routed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers into the foundation's operational USD account at a Panamanian Tier-1 bank. The reference field (RF / /PURP/) should cite 'Aporte de Capital a Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Inversión Directa - VPN SaaS Acquisition' to avoid misclassification. Banks apply OFAC, UN, EU, and SBP sanctions screening; an advance copy of the payment instruction and source-funds evidence must be furnished. For payments originating from regulated PSP aggregators, include the merchant contract and settlement statement to evidence commercial substance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements flow over SWIFT MT103 for supplier or licensing payments, MT202 for interbank-level clearing, and, for physical hardware (servers, network equipment), commercial letters of credit (sight or usance, governed by UCP 600) issued against invoices and transport documentation. USD clearing is executed through U.S. correspondent banks (Fedwire/CHIPS); EUR/GBP disbursements are routed via European and UK correspondent networks. Each disbursement must cite an underlying commercial purpose code and retain invoice, agreement, and KYC evidence to sustain auditability under SBP compliance expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) with licensed Panamanian commercial banks, requiring an embedded ISDA or short-form master agreement
Cross-currency swaps for long-duration licensing contracts, bank-offered and governed by ISDA documentation
Plain-vanilla FX options for treasuries to hedge strategic bid risk in foreign currencies; no meaningful NDF local market exists as Panama is fully dollarized

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (collection agent for the Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January; a 10% surcharge (US$40) applies to payments made 1 February through 31 March; from 1 April the foundation is formally recorded as delinquent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$40 surcharge (total US$440) for late payment; delinquent status blocks issuance of Good Standing certificates and certified copies from the Public Registry; sustained non-payment for approximately three consecutive years exposes the foundation to administrative dissolution and strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Registro Público de Panamá (administered under Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 137 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of incorporation or inclusion in the Register; annual renewal within 30 days following the anniversary of the initial UBO registration; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating fines from US$250 up to US$5,000; outstanding filings block Good Standing certificates; persistent default may be reported to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero for AML enforcement and may support administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (applicable only if the PIF holds an active RUC or derives Panama-source income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year end; deemed not applicable to the standard PIF generating exclusively foreign-source SaaS/VPN subscription revenue with no Panamanian commercial establishment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest and recargos on any omitted Panama-source tax; fines ranging from 20% to 100% of the omitted tax under the Código Fiscal; repeated non-filing may trigger DGI enforcement and administrative penalties against the Foundation Council.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. Audit becomes mandatory only if the foundation conducts regulated commercial or financial activity in Panama requiring DGI audited statements (Panama-source gross income above the B/.300,000 regulatory threshold), or if the Foundation Charter, Regulations, Protector, or Council resolutions require an independent examination.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No specific GAAP mandated by foundation law; books may be maintained under IFRS, US GAAP, or another recognized framework at the Council's election. Where Panama-source commercial activity is taxable, DGI-accepted accounting standards apply. Financial statements are not filed with the Public Registry or the tax authority for a purely passive or foreign-income PIF.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must verify and record all individuals holding directly or indirectly 10% or more of the foundation's assets, rights, or control; where no qualifying individual exists, senior management officials are reported. The annual confirmation is due within 30 days of the registration anniversary, with interim updates within 30 days of any change. The register is confidential and not open to public inspection; access is limited to the Registro Público, tax authorities, and AML supervisors.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) recorded in the Registro Público de Panamá
Foundation Regulations (Reglamento), if maintained separately from the Charter
Register of Foundation Council members, Protector, and qualified beneficiaries
Minute book and resolutions of the Foundation Council
Accounting records and underlying vouchers (retained at the registered office or abroad at the Council's election)
Confidential beneficial ownership file maintained by the resident agent under Law 23 of 2015

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 - US$500 per annum for the Panamanian resident agent, including franchise tax processing and UBO filing coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary independent audit of foundation accounts typically US$2,000 - US$6,000 in Panama City

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate under Article 256 of the Panamanian Tax Code, applied on a strictly territorial basis to Panama-source income only; a reduced progressive rate of 15% may apply to taxpayers with taxable income not exceeding the small-taxpayer threshold established by the DGI).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial exemption for foreign-source income: Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) and other non-resident-invested entities are not taxed on income arising outside Panama, including VPN subscription revenues collected abroad through payment processors such as Stripe and Paymentwall, provided such income is not linked to a commercial establishment, personnel, or source of supply physically located in Panama. PIFs are also exempt from Panama income tax on dividends and capital gains derived from foreign investments and are not subject to controlled-foreign-company attribution. No Panama value-added tax (ITBMS) is chargeable on exported SaaS/digital services, and no net-worth or annual franchise tax is levied on PIFs that do not conduct Panama-source commercial activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 141 - Declaración Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return), filed electronically through the DGI 'Sede Electrónica' portal (e-Tax system, https://dgi.mef.gob.pa) using the taxpayer's RUC and digital signature credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory quarterly advance income tax payments reported on Formulario 142).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, the return and full payment are due no later than 31 March of the year immediately following the close of the fiscal year; for taxpayers authorized to adopt a different fiscal year-end, the return is due within three months after the close of that fiscal year. A one-month extension may be requested from the DGI with documented justification, but payment of the estimated tax liability is still required by the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer registry number, legal name, fiscal address, and registered agent details of the PIF. The form requires the entity's registration date and economic activity code (ISIC 6201).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF must obtain a Panama RUC through its licensed registered agent before filing; the RUC must be active and the foundation must have filed its annual beneficial ownership registry (Law 52 of 2016) with the Registro Público to avoid rejection of the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 1 - Ingresos Brutos de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts derived from activities performed, goods located, or rights exercised within Panama territory. For a VPN network privacy application this includes Panama-domiciled enterprise customers, local server hosting contracts, and any support services physically performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Territorial rule: only these Panama-source amounts are reportable. Foreign subscription revenue routed through Stripe and Paymentwall from non-resident end-users is excluded and should not be booked to this line; a revenue-source ledger identifying customer residency and server location must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 2 - Ingresos Exentos y No Sujetos (Fuente Extranjera)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income lawfully excluded under Panama's territorial system, including foreign-source SaaS license fees, overseas bandwidth and encryption service revenues, and foreign capital gains, with supporting documentation attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF should disclose the foreign-source VPN revenue here and attach a source analysis (contracts, bank statements, IP geolocation logs, and server lease agreements outside Panama). Maintaining this evidence is critical because the DGI may otherwise reclassify the revenue as Panama-source and assess 25% ISR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including overseas server costs, software development, licensing, bandwidth, legal and registered-agent fees, and depreciation of fixed assets related to Panama-source income. Expenses must be justified with invoices and be causally connected to Panama-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF engaged solely in foreign-source VPN sales should allocate only Panama administrative expenses to this line; intercompany charges to/from related entities must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer-pricing analysis to remain deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after subtracting deductible costs and expenses from Panama-source gross income; net capital losses and dividends received from Panama-source subsidiaries are separately treated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF correctly excludes all foreign-source VPN revenue, this line will be zero or negative; a positive figure here triggers the 25% corporate rate and makes the PIF liable for dividend withholding on subsequent distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses from prior fiscal years, deductible to offset current taxable income within the statutory five-year carryforward period. Losses must be supported by audited or certified financial statements and DGI-accepted records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs claiming losses must append a DGI-approved loss schedule and evidence that the losses arise from Panama-source activities; foreign-source losses are not deductible and may not be carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on net taxable income at the 25% corporate rate, or at the reduced progressive rate if the taxpayer qualifies as a small taxpayer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with only foreign-source income reports zero here; if the PIF has incidental Panama-source income, the tax must be paid in full with the filing or via the quarterly advance system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments made on Formulario 142, foreign tax credits (where applicable), and withholding tax credits recognized by the DGI with respect to the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with zero taxes generally have no credits; any credits claimed must be traceable to DGI receipts or tax withholding certificates issued by Panamanian payers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 8 - Saldo por Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount due to the DGI, or refundable credit balance, computed after applying advance payments, withholdings, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid by ACH or DGI-approved electronic channels on or before the filing deadline; refund claims require a completed DGI refund form and may trigger a DGI audit of the territorial source analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 9 - Dividendos Distribuidos y Retención del 10%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividends declared and paid during the tax year, the gross dividend amount, and the 10% dividend withholding tax (or the applicable credit/offset) remitted to the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF distributes profits derived from foreign-source VPN revenues to its founder or beneficiaries, the distribution is not Panamanian-source and no 10% WHT applies; if distributions are made from Panama-source income, the 10% WHT must be remitted with the return, and the naming of each non-resident beneficiary must be disclosed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic surcharge of 10% of the tax due for filing within the first semester of delay, with additional surcharge accumulation beyond that period; moratory interest accrues at 1.5% per month or fraction thereof (18% per annum) on unpaid tax; administrative fines range from USD 50 to USD 5,000 depending on the gravity and persistence of non-compliance; persistent non-filing enables the DGI to make a presumptive assessment, cancel the taxpayer's RUC, and refer the matter for criminal tax-fraud prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 142 - Declaración de Pagos Trimestrales del Impuesto sobre la Renta (Quarterly Advance Income Tax Return), filed through the same DGI Sede Electrónica/e-Tax platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Advance payments are due on the last business day of the month immediately following each fiscal quarter according to the DGI calendar (typically the 15th day of April, July, October, and January for calendar-year taxpayers), with the fourth quarter installment reconciled against the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 1 - Base de Cálculo del Anticipo
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance base computed by the DGI-prescribed method, generally the projected annual Panama-source taxable income or the presumptive-income method for service companies, whichever applies to the taxpayer's election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF whose prior annual return showed only foreign-source VPN income has a zero base and should file a zero Formulario 142 each quarter so that no delinquency flag is raised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installment of the estimated annual ISR, generally equal to one-quarter of the prior year's tax or the amount derived from the presumptive-income rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with Panama-source personnel or servers must remit this installment; failure to do so triggers interest at 1.5% per month plus a 10% underpayment surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 3 - Saldo a Favor o Crédito Trimestral
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit balance carried forward from overpaid prior installments or credits applicable to the quarterly obligation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident entity must protect its credit position by preserving DGI receipts; credits cannot be used to offset unremitted withholding obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment or non-filing of quarterly advances attracts moratory interest of 1.5% per month, a 10% surcharge on the unpaid installments, and administrative fines up to USD 5,000; chronic default triggers mandatory switching of the taxpayer to the presumptive-income regime and DGI enforcement proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed out of Panama-source profits, leviable on distributions to both resident and non-resident shareholders; dividends paid by a PIF exclusively from territorial-exempt foreign-source VPN revenues are not Panama-source income and are therefore not subject to the 10% withholding. In-treaty cases, the DTA may reduce the rate to 5% or exempt the distribution entirely where the beneficial owner is a tax resident of the treaty counterparty and meets limitation-of-benefits conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Invoke treaty relief by: (1) confirming that Panama's applicable double tax agreement (DTA) with the investor's residence jurisdiction is in force and covers the recipient as a resident entitled to benefits; (2) obtaining a Certificate of Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the taxpayer's home tax authority or, for Panama-resident payers, from the DGI; (3) presenting the certificate, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and the entity's foundation charter/registered-agent certificate to the Panamanian withholding agent or the DGI before the payment date to apply the reduced rate at source; (4) where the full 10% has already been withheld, filing a refund claim with the DGI within the statutory refund window (generally the three-year period following the tax year) and submitting the foreign legalization/apostilled certificate of residence plus evidence of Panama tax paid; and (5) retaining the treaty position in the annual Formulario 141 filing, including a disclosure of the dividends and the treaty basis for the reduced or nil WHT. Panama's practical treaty network remains narrow, so the PIF must verify that its beneficiary jurisdiction has a ratified, enforceable DTA before relying on relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory final withholding tax of 10% applies to royalty and IP-license payments made from Panama-source exploitation (including software, trademark, know-how, and encryption-technology licenses); film and audiovisual royalties are typically taxed at 5%. Under active Panama DTAs (for example, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, France, South Korea, Qatar, UAE, Netherlands, Luxembourg), the royalty withholding rate is commonly capped at 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse clauses. Interest: interest paid to non-resident financial institutions on external credit facilities is generally outside the Panama-source nexus and is not subject to withholding; where the interest is demonstrably Panama-source, the statutory ceiling is 10% and treaty rates generally reduce it to 5%-10%, again requiring a valid Certificate of Residence and economic-substance documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory preparation and filing of the Local File and Master File under Panama's transfer-pricing regime (Decreto Ejecutivo 125 de 2019 and the DGI TP annexes to the ISR return) where annual gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000 or where cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; a TP disclosure annex is required for any related-party transaction above USD 200,000, and the PIF must sustain arm's-length pricing for intercompany SaaS licensing, VPN infrastructure leases, and management service fees. The threshold is expressed in US dollars/balboas, reflecting the dollarized Panamanian currency.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime applicable to PIFs, and a PIF holding only foreign-source VPN subscription income is not required to demonstrate substantial local activity. However, the territorial exemption is conditional: the DGI may recharacterize the PIF as a Panama-resident commercial operator if VPN network management, developer personnel, decision-making, or servers are located in Panama. To protect the exemption, the PIF should maintain a Panama registered office, a resident registered agent, a foundation council (or protector) with formal minutes, complete accounting books, a beneficial-ownership file filed under Law 52 of 2016, and documentary proof that customers, servers, payment flows, and operational management are located outside Panama. The OECD Harmful Tax Practices framework and EU listings also pressure Panama to require adequate substance for entities claiming tax benefits; a no-substance PIF routed through Panama banks faces account termination and enhanced AML scrutiny.
